paper.title: Sign Language Recognition: A Deep Survey

description: A broad survey of visual deep-learning approaches to isolated and continuous sign recognition, covering input modalities, datasets, methods and open challenges.
reason: Meets M1–M3 as a broader review with qualifying CSLR coverage. Section 7 and Table 8 (pp.18–20) compare Pu et al. (2018) and Cui et al. (2019) by methods, datasets and reported error rates, meeting the project-specific two-study threshold.

M1.reason: The abstract and introduction explicitly synthesize prior vision-based deep-learning research; Sections 4–8 review existing methods.

M2.reason: Section 7 and Table 8 compare at least two distinct prior CSLR studies, Pu et al. (2018) and Cui et al. (2019), satisfying the full-text threshold.

M3.reason: Sections 7.1 and 7.3 and Table 8 explicitly cover RGB video and RGB/optical-flow approaches to CSLR.

evidence.passage: Taxonomy covers isolated and continuous recognition, datasets, applications and hybrid vision-based deep-learning models.

evidence.locator: PDF p.1, Abstract; p.3, Introduction and Section 2
evidence.passage: The authors explicitly review vision-based deep-learning approaches and propose a taxonomy covering isolated and continuous sign recognition, datasets, applications and research challenges.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.18–19, Section 7, especially Sections 7.1 and 7.3; p.20, Table 8; pp.26–27, references
evidence.passage: Section 7 discusses prior continuous-recognition methods. Section 7.1 describes Pu et al. (2018), combining 3D-ResNet, dilated CNN and CTC on RGB video; Section 7.3 describes Cui et al. (2019), combining CNN/Bi-LSTM, iterative training, RGB and optical flow. Table 8 compares their modalities, models, datasets and reported error rates, including PHOENIX-Weather 2014 and SIGNUM. These are two distinct prior CSLR studies.

The discussion distinguishes isolated recognition from sequence recognition and temporal alignment. It identifies feature extraction and alignment as central issues and proposes attention, multiple modalities, structured spatiotemporal models and sign-language prior knowledge as future directions. Table 8 includes visual RGB-video methods.
